title: Push a rover that cannot be lifted across a washout by taking it at an angle
instruction: The rover has lost power. Push it across the washout to the pad without lifting it.
context: A rigid four-wheeled vehicle crosses a gap narrower than its tyres only if no axle is over the gap at once. Taken square, this 14 kg rover (free-rolling wheels, unpowered steering) drops both front tyres into the 5 cm washout and wedges, and the arms cannot lift an axle out. Taken at about 30 degrees, one wheel is over the gap at a time and the other three carry it level. The angle has to be set by steering at a standstill and walking it round, then the rover walked across and handed from one arm to the other to reach the pad. A robot crew does this where a stranded field rover cannot be reached by people. Unlike #1490 (a cart tipped onto its big wheels to clear a sill) nothing is tipped or lifted; the line taken decides it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Track: an earth-brown slab 3.2 cm thick (painted plywood) from x 13 to 70, y -45 to 56; across it a washout cut 3 cm deep from y 15 to 20 (its floor dark brown); a white tape line (6 mm) across the track at y 22, the start of the pad (y 22 to 56). Rover: a rover built for the rig at the size of a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M body shell in polycarbonate, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, on an aluminium chassis with steel axles and about 13 kg of lead (1.15 L) cast to fill the body between and over the axles: 14 kg in all, centre of mass 5.5 cm up; hard rubber tyres 5.6 cm across, the front pair crowned (rounded tread), the rear flat; the front axle a turntable pivoting at its middle (both front wheels turn together); driveshafts removed so its wheels roll freely; steering servo unpowered, so the front wheels stay where they are put; its origin (midway between the axles) at (20, -12), heading +y (toward the robot's left), square to the gap, front wheels straight. Tow tabs: dark grey 3D-printed PLA tabs 5.0 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm on the middle of each bumper, 4.5 cm up, each with a post 1 cm across and 3 cm tall at its tip; the rear tab's end at y -29.9. Steering tiller: a red 3D-printed PLA pin 1 cm across and 4 cm tall (top 11.2 cm up) on an arm of the turntable axle reaching forward under the bonnet's lip, 4.5 cm ahead of the axle's pivot, so it swings with the front wheels.
scoring: 0 if at any time both tyres of an axle are more than 1 cm above the ground under them at once (the rover lifted; over the washout the ground is taken at the track's surface), or both tyres of an axle are over the washout at once (the middle of each tread's lowest line between the washout's edges: taken square, or carried across level). Otherwise, at the end, after 2 s with the rover at rest (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s) and released (no point of either gripper, and no point along either arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover, its wheels and steering): 1.0 all four tyres beyond the washout (every point of each tread past its far edge) and on the pad (past y 22 cm, the near edge of the pad's tape line, inside the track, the lowest point within 5 mm of the surface); 0.25 at least one tyre beyond the washout; 0 otherwise. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Set the rover back on its marks at the near end, square to the washout, front wheels straight.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control; rigid suspension. 14 kg rover (centre of mass 5.5 cm up), the mass at which an arm cannot lift an axle. Free wheels with drag; turntable front axle (+-30 deg) held by 0.15 N m of friction for the unpowered servo. Crowned front tyres touch at a point, as built; flat treads would stop a hand steering at a standstill. A tyre's edge barely turns the steering, so a tiller pin is fitted.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0, 2 runs (the arms moved about the rover's sides; it was not steered or moved to the gap); demo: 1.0
